chapter: Chicago friends: Tesch, Stacy and Wettling
title: Wettling's cowboy outfit from Paul Whiteman
summary: Freeman tells the story of Wettling wearing the sheriff's cowboy outfit on drunks in New York gangster bars.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: He didn't really need very much. He like Dave Tough and Bix and many, many others didn't need very much to set them off. And they went completely out of their minds and didn't know what they were saying and what they were doing, and I write this story in the book, the book published in Ireland, which I just mentioned, opens up with a George Wettling story and I tell about the time George Wettling was playing with Paul Whiteman.
Now, when Paul Whiteman went on a drunk, it was a big, and he was a big, strong man and they were out in Texas and when you were honored in Texas, it was usually,

you were made a sheriff, they gave you an authentic sheriff's badge and they gave Paul Whiteman and George a complete set, a cowboy set, a complete outfit of cowboy clothing, the ten-gallon hat, the dungarees, the boots, the belt with synthetic bullets and a gun that actually worked, but with no real bullets, and a holster for it.

Now when George Wettling went on one of his drunks when he didn't know what he was doing in New York, he would go around, he would put this outfit on and go into these tough bars that were gangster-ridden and take out his gun and say, 'Why don't you so and sos go back west where men are men?' He was completely out of his mind and if it hadn't been for certain of these underworld characters who knew him he would have been killed. They would have really given him a terrible going over.
But this was George Wettling. Of course, it has nothing to do with the music, but this is what happened to him when he drank.
